$ rea --help
exit: 0
--- stdout
rea@<version> — Reverse engineer anything from your terminal or agent.

Usage: rea <command> [options]

Start with:
  inspect-artifact <path>                Identify any file; prints the next probes
  analyze <path>                         Overview of a native app
  analyze-javascript-application <path>  A JavaScript or Electron app on disk
  list-browser-targets <endpoint>        Pages of a running browser (CDP)
  guidance --query <words>               Search REA's guides
  doctor                                 Check providers and agent setup

Families (rea help <family> lists its commands):
  start        Set up, check and update REA; guides; providers
  artifact     Identify, unpack and inspect files and packages of any format
  native       Decompile, search, cross-reference and trace native code
  binary       ELF, PE, Mach-O facts: imports, hardening, debug info, crashes
  debug        gdb, rizin, objdump, Cutter, Frida; observe native calls and UI
  managed      .NET (PE/CLI) assemblies and their native boundaries
  android      Android and Flutter apps: APK, DEX, resources, JEB
  adb          A connected Android device through adb
  firmware     Firmware images, UEFI volumes and NVRAM
  web          Live pages and bundles: capture, network, scripts, sources
  javascript   JavaScript and Electron apps: analysis, recovery, runtime
  captures     Packet captures and signal recordings
  desktop      Desktop applications and processes: capture, state, export
  application  Whole applications: versions, API contracts, feature traces
  evidence     Saved Evidence: views, bundles, export, import, compare
  environment  Agent environments: build, serve, compare, export
  clone-run    Rebuild a web application under a referee (this fork only)

More: rea <command> --help (one command), rea help all (every command, one line each),
rea help options (--json, --format, --filter-output, --token-limit, ...),
rea --llms (manifest), rea completions <shell>, rea mcp.
<end>

<end>
